AWPTCM-T33370.objective:
• When two-step authentication is enabled with MAC as the first method and WEB as the second method, a correct MAC address at the first step transitions the supplicant to the "Connecting" state awaiting the second-step WEB authentication.
  • Invalid MAC at the first step places the supplicant in the HELD state for the duration of the quiet-period.
  • Invalid WEB credentials within the max-auth-fail limit at the second step place the supplicant in the "Reauthenticating" state, allowing further attempts.
  • Invalid WEB credentials at the max-auth-fail count at the second step place the supplicant in the HELD state for the quiet-period.
  • Successful completion of the second-step WEB authentication results in the supplicant reaching the Authenticated state.
  • Correct log messages are generated at the appropriate times for success and failure of each step (first MAC and second WEB), including IP and MAC details for WEB.
  • The "auth two-step enable" command is accepted, appears in running-config, persists after save and reboot, and can be disabled with the "no" form.
  • The "show auth two-step supplicant" (and brief) commands accurately report two-step information including firstMethod (mac), secondMethod (web), per-supplicant status for each step, and counts.
  • The "auth-mac password" command works correctly for two-step MAC first / WEB second (password can match MAC or be RADIUS configured).
  • The maximum number of supplicants supported for two-step auth (1st MAC / 2nd WEB) is correctly enforced.
  • Repeated execution of two-step authentication using 1st MAC / 2nd WEB does not cause crashes, hangs, or errors.
  • RADIUS integration and MAC address list (allow/deny) function correctly in the two-step MAC first / WEB second context.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.

Enable two-step authentication (auth two-step enable) together with MAC auth and WEB auth. Configure optional auth-mac password. Verify the enable command and "no" form work, persist after reboot, and appear correctly in running-config.

Connect a supplicant. Perform Two-Step with 1st step MAC (correct MAC) followed by 2nd step WEB (correct credentials). Verify transition through Connecting state to final Authenticated state. Confirm "show auth two-step supplicant" reports firstMethod=mac, secondMethod=web, and step statuses. Verify auth-mac password works if used.

Test failure paths: invalid MAC at 1st step (expect HELD + quiet-period), correct MAC then invalid WEB within max-auth-fail (expect Reauthenticating), then full max-auth-fail (expect HELD). Verify logs are generated at the correct steps for WEB as 2nd.
Verify correct success and failure log messages are produced for each step (MAC first and WEB second), including proper formatting with IP/MAC for WEB logs.
Test the supported maximum number of supplicants for this two-step combination (1st MAC / 2nd WEB). Confirm enforcement and that excess attempts are handled correctly.
Repeat the full 1st-MAC / 2nd-WEB two-step sequence multiple times (including logout). Confirm no crashes, hangs, or unexpected errors occur.
Confirm MAC address list (allow/deny) and RADIUS integration work in the two-step MAC first + WEB second context.
